This exceptional diversity is shaped by New Mexico’s size and the intersection of several major ecoregions, including the Colorado Plateau, Southern Rocky Mountains, Arizona–New Mexico Mountains, Central and Southern Short‑grass Prairies, the Chihuahuan Desert, and the Western High Plains. Together, these varied landscapes sustain a remarkable array of wildlife, ranging from large mammals like pronghorn and black bears down to smaller species like deer mice and desert whiptails. The Bureau of Land Management manages 13.5 million acres of public land across New Mexico, Oklahoma, Texas, and Kansas. Managing wildlife across such varied habitats requires a coordinated and science‑based approach. BLM biologists and other field staff work alongside Tribal nations, state and federal agencies, community partners, and conservation organizations to maintain healthy ecosystems and support long‑term habitat resilience. Fort Stanton Cave, an extensive limestone cave within the NCA is over 26 miles long making it the third longest cave in New Mexico, the 20th longest cave in the U.S., the 76th longest in the world, and the largest cave managed by the BLM. Modern-day cavers have been exploring its passages for over 50 years and continue their explorations and study as part of the Fort Stanton Cave Study Project (FSCSP). The FSCSP is a non-profit organization whose mission is to conduct and promote exploration, public education, scientific research, and environmentally sound management of the caves and karst within and surrounding the NCA. As NPR Music's Daoud Tyler-Ameen and WRTI's Nate Chinen discuss, his new album Beautifully Broken is a powerful (and sometimes overwhelming) portrait of recovery and empathy for those grappling with addiction. Also on the show this week: The second album from punk teens The Linda Lindas feels like confirmation of a promising career; Samara Joy and Immanuel Wilkins put two different approaches to the modern jazz vocal album on display; E L U C I D combines influences from Miles Davis to Public Enemy into a harrowing experience of modern indie rap and Charli XCX's remix album leads us to consider the tradition of artists reworking their own songs. pages.text: New Neanderthal Genome Shows How Ancient DNA Affects Your Health | National Geographic This reconstruction of a Neanderthal female unveiled in 2008 was the first made using ancient DNA evidence. Photograph by Joe McNally, Nat Geo Image Collection New Clues to How Neanderthal Genes Affect Your Health A genome from a female found in Croatia shows how conditions from schizophrenia to arthritis are influenced by our ancient human cousins. By Michelle Z. Donahue Published October 5, 2017 • 6 min read If your arthritis is bad today or you’re slathering on aloe for an early autumn sunburn, Neanderthals may be partly to blame. Scientists announced today the second complete, high-quality sequencing of a Neanderthal genome , made using the 52,000-year-old bones of a female found in the Vindija cave in Croatia. 4:05 Together with the genomes from another Neanderthal woman and a host of modern humans, a suite of analyses is yielding new clues about how DNA from Neanderthals contributed to our genetic makeup and might still be affecting us today. For instance, one new study appearing in the journal Science suggests that Neanderthal genes contribute 1.8 to 2.6 percent of the total genetic makeup for people of Eurasian ancestry. That’s slightly up from a previous estimate of 1.5 to 2.1 percent. (Find out about the first solid DNA evidence that Neanderthals and modern humans interbred .) pages.description: A steady stream of weight loss drugs, which mimic naturally occurring hormones, are in the pipeline. This competition may finally lead to lower prices and greater supplies of these highly effective drugs, and maybe replace some injectables with pills.
pages.text: New obesity drugs are coming. Here's how they could change everything. | National Geographic Premium SCIENCE MIND, BODY, WONDER New obesity drugs are coming. Here's how they could change everything. A steady stream of weight loss drugs, which mimic naturally occurring hormones, are in the pipeline. This competition may finally lead to lower prices and greater supplies of these highly effective drugs, and maybe replace some injectables with pills. Ozempic (above) was not the first of the hormone-mimicking drugs to hit the market, but it was the first to become a household name as celebrities shared their weight loss success from its off-label use on social media. Photograph by Jaap Arriens, NurPhoto/Getty Images By Tara Haelle Published December 22, 2023 • 13 min read The recent approval of another obesity drug , Zepbound, expands the options for medications to manage weight, but it comes with the same cost and access challenges that plague other weight loss drugs in its class. The drugs in this class are agonists , or mimics, of natural gut hormones that affect the body’s metabolism and hunger signals in the brain. But the currently approved drugs, synthetic versions of these hormones, are large molecules that are expensive and time-consuming to manufacture, which has meant high prices for consumers and growing drug shortages. Further, most of these drugs are injections, rather than oral pills, and usually require refrigeration for storage. pages.title: New Orleans cruise ship collision: All passengers rescued in 'miracle on the Mississippi' British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: The collision leaves 32 people in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for.
pages.text: New Orleans cruise ship collision: All passengers rescued in 'miracle on the Mississippi' Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All passengers rescued after New Orleans cruise ship collision 3 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Ana Faguy Watch: Cruise ship seen sinking after collision with cargo ship in New Orleans Some 130 people on a cruise ship docked in New Orleans have been rescued after it was struck by a tanker. The cruise ship, American Heritage, was left lying on its side in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel Atlantic Asphalt. The collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for. Officials hailed it as a "miracle on the Mississippi". The exact cause of the crash remains under investigation, but US Coast Guard Capt Melanie Burnham said: "There seems to be some type of a loss of steering." New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference on Friday that all credit in the rescue effort should go to first responders who "literally jumped right in to help". "We have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," Moreno said. Calls about the collision began around 13:30 EST (18:30 GMT) on Friday, when people began trying to help passengers escape the boat as it took on water, Port of New Orleans chief Melanie Montroll told the news conference. pages.description: Laser scans and other evidence show the Maya persisted in rural areas long after big cities collapsed.
pages.text: New research challenges the idea that the Maya civilization collapsed | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE Why the idea that the Maya civilization ‘collapsed’ is wrong Laser scans and other evidence show the Maya persisted in rural areas long after big cities collapsed. The Maya are known for their impressive pyramid complexes, like this one known as El Castillo at Chichén Itzá. But local towns and villages sustained these urban areas, and new population estimates of those areas are bringing up questions about whether the Maya really collapsed. Photograph by Paul Nicklen, Nat Geo Image Collection By Joshua Rapp Learn Published December 26, 2024 The Maya created great kingdoms that ruled over tens of thousands of people for centuries in Mesoamerica. But as elaborate capitals like Chichén Itzá and Mayapan and the elites that controlled them rose and fell, the surrounding population that lived in the rural areas around them didn’t change for centuries. The textbook timeline of the Maya civilization goes like this: The culture reached its height , known as the Classic period, between A.D. 200 and 900. Over the next century, urban centers fell apart. By some accounts, the Maya vanished, and scientists have implicated climate, overpopulation, and political unrest in their mysterious demise. While the Maya bounced back during the Postclassic period from A.D. 900 until the arrival of Spanish colonizers around 1540, it supposedly never reached its previous strength. She says she put the game's release on her leave request form which was approved, she told BBC News, despite the fact her boss "doesn't know what GTA 6 is". She's far from the only one. For the game's launch day, HR software company BrightHR looked at absence data from more than 1.2 million employees from 70,000 businesses across the UK. The new base for the Air Ambulance Service (TAAS) will be built on land off Swinford Road in Catthorpe, Leicestershire. It comes after the closure of Coventry Airport in June this year, where the charity had operated from for more than 23 years. Harborough District Council approved the plans for the base, which will include two helipads, a hangar, training facilities, rest areas and a gym, at a planning committee meeting on Wednesday. TAAS said it had been given permission to continue to operate from Coventry Airport, despite its permanent closure, until the new base had been built. SCIENCE LAELAPS Newfound Fossil Octopus and Squid Were Giants By Riley Black Published March 10, 2015 • 4 min read A good fossil squid is hard to find. The invertebrates are too squishy to leave much behind, and only in truly exceptional circumstances do paleontologists get to see much more than the chitinous supports the cephalopods kept on the inside. Octopus are even more confounding. Without any remnants of an internal shell, the eight-armed quick-change artists are like prehistoric ghosts. But do not despair. The jaws of ancient coleoids give us reason for hope, and have just revealed a pair of prehistoric cephalopods that may have rivaled today’s ocean giants in size. Described by Kazushige Tanabe and colleagues in Acta Palaeontologica Polonica , the two lower jaws were found in roughly 80 million year old rock around Hokkaido, Japan’s Haboro-futamata Dam. Both were preserved in three-dimensional detail, providing Tanabe and coworkers with enough anatomical clues to figure out that they were left behind by previously-unknown species. Octopus and squid beaks can be very informative fossils. That’s because marine biologists have spent a great deal of time studying the chitinous beaks of modern cephalopods. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/services-resources/software/nfiq-2 SOFTWARE NFIQ 2 Version 2.3.0 Type of Software Biometric fingerprint quality assessment Last Updated 10/01/2024 NIST Author Elham Tabassi Other Contributors Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA) MITRE Fraunhofer IGD Hochschule Darmstadt (h_da) Secunet GitHub Contributors ​​​​​​About NIST Fingerprint Image Quality (NFIQ) 2 is open source software that links image quality of optical and ink 500 PPI fingerprints to operational recognition performance. This allows quality values to be tightly defined and then numerically calibrated, which in turn allows for the standardization needed to support a worldwide deployment of fingerprint sensors with universally interpretable image qualities. NFIQ 2 quality features are formally standardized as part of ISO/IEC 29794-4 and serve as the reference implementation of the standard. Most, but not all of them, have improved their chances Doug Farrar Wed 11 Nov 2026 04.00 EST Last modified on Wed 11 Nov 2026 10.30 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The Vikings get the QB they desperately need After what happened Monday night, the Minnesota Vikings had to do this. In a dispiriting loss to the Buffalo Bills, the Vikings saw their tremendous defense go to waste, as Carson Wentz completed eight of 25 passes for 81 yards, no touchdowns, two interceptions and a passer rating of 8.9. It was one of the worst quarterback performances in recent history , and it continued a run of recent QB futility for the Vikings, from JJ McCarthy to Kyler Murray to Wentz. Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores is out-scheming every other coach in the league with his laboratory of blitzes and coverages. But it’s starting to matter less and less, because opposing offenses know they can wait that defense out when there’s no juice on the other side of the ball. Close nicofr77's Diary À portée de train : une carte des boucles vélo accessibles en train, depuis 60 villes Posted by nicofr77 on 2 October 2026 in French (Français) . Last updated on 4 October 2026. Je publie sur Tisseur de Voies, le site où je calcule des boucles vélo avec retour en train, une carte qui répond à une question simple : depuis ma ville, jusqu’où puis-je partir à vélo en prenant un seul train ? On choisit une ville parmi 60 et une durée de train aller, de 0 à 4 heures. La carte montre en rose les véloroutes des boucles qu’on peut rejoindre, et en bleu les gares atteintes, plus foncées quand elles sont proches. Ici, Paris avec une heure de train : 1 763 boucles, contre 323 qui partent des gares parisiennes. Une boucle, c’est un itinéraire à vélo d’une gare à une autre sur des véloroutes balisées, avec un train pour rentrer. Elle compte dès qu’un train aller atteint l’une de ses gares dans la durée choisie. Un classement des 60 villes accompagne la carte : Paris, Strasbourg et Lille en tête, Brest et Quimper en queue. Les véloroutes viennent d’OpenStreetMap et du référentiel national des véloroutes, le fond de carte d’OpenStreetMap. Les durées sortent des horaires publiés en open data par la SNCF, Île-de-France Mobilités, la Région Sud et les Chemins de fer de la Corse : pour chaque trajet, la durée médiane de la ligne la plus rapide qui circule au moins une fois par jour. Seuls les trains sans changement comptent.
